topic: A CDN during a flash sale — why 400,000 people downloading the same product photos from one server turned the API into a file server, and how Azure Front Door serves them from edge locations near each user instead.

title.sub: A flash sale turns the API into a file server.

stageHtml:
📱  Chennai ⬜ loading…
📱  Mumbai ⬜ loading…
📱  Delhi ⬜ loading…
↕↕↕
no copy nearby Chennai —
no copy nearby Mumbai —
no copy nearby Delhi —
↕↕↕
App Serviceserving every photo itself 0 GB/s
🖼️ biryani-99.jpg · 350 KB
SALE 400,000 people open the same page.
Same bytes?
Serve them from the edge.
🌍 CDN: files ⚡ Redis: data
📌 Azure Front Door (CDN)

stages.title: One photo, 400,000 phones
stages.desc: Four photos per page, 350 KB each. Everybody opens the page at 12:00.
stages.narration: Four hundred thousand phones. Four photos each. One point six million downloads.

stages.title: Every download hits one server
stages.desc: Chennai, Mumbai, Delhi. All of them pull the same bytes from App Service.
stages.status: App Service → every phone, every photo
stages.narration: Every download comes from one server, in one region, across the whole country.

stages.title: The API became a file server
stages.desc: The servers spent the sale shipping bytes that never change.
stages.narration: The servers become file servers, shipping bytes that never change.

stages.title: Same bytes, every time
stages.desc: The photo was identical for all 400,000 people.
stages.narration: And the photo was identical for every single person.

stages.title: Put a copy near the users
stages.desc: Azure Front Door keeps copies at edge locations. The original moves to Blob Storage.
stages.narration: The fix: copies near the users, at Azure Front Door edge locations.

stages.title: First download: fetch once
stages.desc: Chennai's edge has no copy yet, so it fetches the photo from Blob Storage one time.
stages.status: Chennai edge · MISS → Blob Storage → cached
stages.narration: First tap in Chennai. The edge fetches the photo once, and keeps it.

stages.title: Everyone else: from the edge
stages.desc: The next 10,000 people in each city never reach your servers.
stages.status: HIT · nearest edge · origin sees 3 in 100
stages.narration: Everyone after that gets it from the edge. Your servers barely see them.

stages.title: Never on the CDN
stages.desc: Carts, checkout, stock left. A CDN gives everyone the same answer.
stages.status: CDN = same response for every user
stages.narration: Never cache carts, checkout or stock. A CDN gives everyone the same answer.

stages.title: New photo? New URL
stages.desc: Save it under a new name. Edges and phones fetch it fresh. No purge.
stages.narration: Photo changed? Give it a new file name. Edges and phones fetch it fresh.

stages.title: Serve the same bytes from the edge
stages.desc: CDN for files. Redis for data. The database for the truth.
stages.narration: Same bytes for everyone? Serve them from the edge.

end.title: Same bytes? Serve them from the edge.
end.sub: Put files behind a CDN like Azure Front Door, and give every changed file a new URL.

post.caption:
Picture a flash sale that does not fail on logic. It fails on photos. 🍛

400,000 people open the same product page at 12:00. Four photos each, 350 KB a photo. That is 1.6 million downloads, and every single one comes from the app's own App Service, in one region.

Grey boxes where the photos should be. An API spending the biggest sale of the year as a file server.

THE REAL PROBLEM
The photo was identical for everyone. Same bytes, from far away, every time.

THE FIX: A CDN
Move the photos to Blob Storage and put Azure Front Door in front of them. Front Door keeps copies at edge locations near your users.
1. The first person in a city asks. The edge fetches the photo once.
2. Everyone after that gets it from the edge.
3. Your origin sees about 3 requests in every 100.

Upload with a long cache header:

az storage blob upload-batch \
  --account-name stassets --destination images \
  --source ./images --auth-mode login \
  --content-cache-control "public, max-age=31536000, immutable"

PUT ON A CDN
Product photos, JS and CSS bundles, fonts, icons, promo banners.

NEVER ON A CDN
Carts, checkout, addresses, stock left, live prices, anything behind a login. A CDN gives everyone the same answer — cache one person's cart and the next person sees it.

WHEN THE PHOTO CHANGES
Give it a new URL (put a hash in the filename). Purging only fixes the CDN; the phone keeps its own copy by URL. A new URL fixes both.

NOTE: classic Azure CDN retires on 30 September 2027. On Azure, "CDN" now means Azure Front Door Standard or Premium.

Full incident write-up: blog.msdevbuild.com/blog/azure-front-door-cdn-flash-sale

Follow for Azure & Cloud Engineering tips.
